ANALYSIS: No fusion trials yet. Single-model baselines cluster at 0.80-0.82 macro AUROC, with H-optimus-1 best (~0.823). Metadata alone is weak (0.60) and adds little. The embeddings are high-dimensional (1536-2560) and n is small (134 per training fold), so strong regularisation matters.
REASONING: Start with a robust, low-variance anchor: late fusion with mean_prob. It averages three well-regularised per-model logistic regressions. This usually gives a reliable ensemble gain when the models are of comparable strength and partly decorrelated. C=0.01 on standardised high-dimensional features is a sensible strong-regularisation default. No PCA and no L2 norm keeps it simple. meta_weight=1 because metadata helps little.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.83-0.84, a modest gain over the best single model, from lower variance. If it is no better than about 0.82, the models' errors are highly correlated or C is mis-set. In that case I would probe C (0.001 vs 0.1) and early fusion with balance_blocks next.

ANALYSIS: Late fusion with mean_prob at C=0.01 gives 0.830, only slightly above the best single model, H-optimus-1 at 0.824. Lepidic (0.75) and Papillary (0.73) are the weak classes. The effects of regularisation strength and fusion method are still untested.
REASONING: Early fusion is a structurally different and untested alternative. A joint linear model can use complementary features across models, which late averaging cannot. With roughly 5600 dimensions and only 134 patients, strong regularisation is needed. So I choose C=0.001 with balance_blocks=true, so that Virchow2's larger block does not dominate, and keep meta_weight at 1 for comparability.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.83–0.85, possibly with better Lepidic and Papillary AUROC. If it does not beat trial #1 clearly, joint concatenation adds nothing over averaging. In that case I would go back to tuning late fusion (C, the combine method, L2 normalisation).

ANALYSIS: Late mean_prob (0.830) and early balanced concat (0.829) are essentially tied, and both sit only slightly above the best single model, H-optimus-1 (0.824). Per-class AUROCs are nearly identical across the two fusions, and Lepidic and Papillary are the weak classes. Regularisation strength has not been explored: late was run only at C=0.01, early only at C=0.001.
REASONING: With 134 training patients and 1536–2560-d inputs, the C value per base model probably matters more than the choice of fusion rule. Before tuning combiners, I should check whether the late base models are over- or under-regularised. Moving one step stronger (C=0.001), with everything else fixed, isolates that single knob. Stronger shrinkage often helps mean-pooled embeddings at this sample size, and averaging probabilities can also benefit from smoother base predictions.
EXPECTED: I expect a gain of about 0.005–0.01 if C=0.01 was overfitting. If AUROC drops or stays flat, the optimum is at C=0.01 or weaker, and the next step would be C=0.1 or changing the combiner (stack/learned_weights).

ANALYSIS: Late mean_prob at C=0.01 (0.8298) edges out the best single model (H-optimus-1, 0.8236). Early fusion at C=0.001 is equivalent, and late fusion at C=0.001 is worse, so stronger regularisation hurts in late fusion. Weak classes are Lepidic and Papillary (~0.73-0.75). Higher C, PCA, L2 normalisation and the other combiners are all untested.
REASONING: The C direction is the most informative single axis. C=0.001 lost 0.0075, which suggests the optimum may lie at C≥0.01. Testing C=0.1 with everything else fixed tells us whether less shrinkage helps the per-model classifiers before I explore combiners or preprocessing. Keeping mean_prob isolates the effect of C.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.83-0.84 if weaker regularisation helps; a clear gain would be accepted. If it falls or stays flat, C=0.01 is near-optimal for late fusion. In that case I will hold C fixed and test L2 normalisation, PCA and the stack or mean_logit combiners.

ANALYSIS: Late mean_prob at C=0.01 (0.830) is the current best, only ~0.006 above the best single model (hoptimus1, 0.824). Early fusion with balanced blocks scored about the same. C=0.01 looks like the optimum for late fusion, since both 0.001 and 0.1 are worse. Lepidic and Papillary (~0.73) are the weak classes in every trial.
REASONING: With C now settled, the untested preprocessing knobs are the most likely source of a clear gain. Per-slide L2 normalisation of mean-pooled embeddings often helps linear probes: it removes slide-level scale and stain/intensity effects that a mean pool carries. Testing it at the known-good late/C=0.01/mean_prob setting changes one variable only, so the result is attributable to that knob.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of roughly 0.835-0.845, with the main gains in Lepidic and Papillary, which would clear the ~0.005 threshold. If there is no gain, L2 normalisation is redundant once features are standardised. In that case I would next try PCA (32/64) or the stack and learned_weights combiners.

ANALYSIS: Late mean_prob at C=0.01 (0.830) is the best so far. It is only about +0.006 over hoptimus1 alone. The C value is bracketed: both 0.001 and 0.1 are worse. L2 norm did not help. Early fusion at C=0.001 with balanced blocks ties with it. The weakest classes are Lepidic and Papillary (~0.73), which suggests the limit is shared signal, not the fusion rule.
REASONING: The combine rule is still untested. hoptimus1 is the strongest single model, so learned_weights could tilt the weights toward it. Stack could also recalibrate per class. However, stacking a 21-feature model on 134 patients is risky. PCA is another open axis that could cut noise in the high-dimensional blocks. I'll test PCA=64 inside late fusion with the known-good C=0.01 and mean_prob. Reducing to 64-d before logistic regression changes the bias-variance tradeoff, so it could give a clear gain rather than a tiny one. It also answers whether dimensionality reduction helps at all.
EXPECTED: If PCA denoises, AUROC should reach about 0.835-0.84 and exceed the roughly 0.005 threshold. Note that C was tuned for the full dimension, so the optimal C may shift with fewer features. If AUROC drops, the discriminative signal is spread across many dimensions. I would then drop PCA and move on to the combine rules (learned_weights, stack).

ANALYSIS: Late mean_prob fusion at C=0.01 (0.8298) is only marginally above the best single model (H-optimus-1, 0.8236). Early fusion ties with it, and moving C away from 0.01 hurts. L2 normalisation and PCA=64 change nothing measurable. Weak classes (Lepidic about 0.74, Papillary about 0.72) do not move under any linear variant tried, which suggests the linear late/early knobs are close to saturated.
REASONING: The gated method is completely untested and is the only one that could plausibly add something new: per-patient weighting of the models, which might help the classes where the models disagree. To reduce its overfitting risk with 134 training patients, I use strong regularisation: PCA=64 per model (this matched no-PCA in late fusion), a small hidden size of 32, dropout 0.5, weight decay 0.1, a moderate 200 epochs at lr 0.001, and 3 averaged seeds. Untried late combiners (stack, learned_weights, meta_weight) remain as follow-ups.
EXPECTED: Most likely AUROC of about 0.81-0.83, i.e. no accepted gain. A clear gain above the threshold (about +0.005-0.01), especially on Lepidic or Papillary, would show that adaptive gating helps. If it underperforms or has a larger fold SD, I conclude gating overfits at this sample size. I would then return to late fusion and test stack, learned_weights and meta_weight=3.

ANALYSIS: Late mean_prob fusion at C=0.01 (0.8298) is about +0.006 over the best single model. Varying C, L2 norm, PCA, early fusion and a regularised gated net all landed within noise of it or below. The base-learner settings look saturated near C=0.01, and the weak classes (Lepidic about 0.75, Papillary about 0.73) are consistent across every variant.
REASONING: The main untested axis is the combiner. Equal-weight averaging cannot reweight models per class, and metadata only enters weakly through each base model. A stacking logistic regression on the base log-probabilities plus age/sex can learn class-specific trust in each model, for example where gated beat late on Cribriform and Micropapillary. I am keeping the best base settings (C=0.01, no PCA, no L2 norm) and using a moderate stack_C=0.1 to limit overfitting from the inner-CV predictions.
EXPECTED: A plausible gain of +0.005 to +0.015 AUROC if per-class reweighting helps. If it does not beat the threshold or comes out lower, then with about 134 patients the stacker's variance cancels any gain. I would then switch to simpler combiners (learned_weights, mean_logit) or metadata weighting rather than more flexible fusion.

ANALYSIS: Late mean_prob fusion at C=0.01 (0.830) leads; early fusion, PCA64, L2 norm, gated and stacking all failed to beat it clearly. C=0.01 looks optimal, since both 0.001 and 0.1 were worse. Lepidic (0.75) and Papillary (0.73) remain the weak classes. Metadata added about +0.006 to +0.010 to uni2h and virchow2 alone. In all fusion trials so far, though, meta_weight was 1, so at C=0.01 the age/sex columns were heavily shrunk.
REASONING: Metadata is the one untested axis with a plausible independent signal: meta alone scores 0.60 AUROC, and it is complementary to image features. With meta_weight=10, the two standardised meta columns get roughly 100x less effective L2 penalty (about C=1 for meta), while the image features keep the proven C=0.01. This changes one knob from the best configuration, so the result is interpretable. It also adds only two weakly penalised features, so overfitting risk is small.
EXPECTED: I expect a gain of about +0.005 to +0.015 AUROC, mostly in classes linked to age or sex (possibly In situ, Lepidic or Solid), plus a modest balanced-accuracy increase. If the gain is null or negative, metadata adds nothing beyond the image embeddings in fusion. I would then leave meta_weight at 1 and test the combiner instead (learned_weights or mean_logit).

ANALYSIS: Fusion gives ~0.83 vs the best single model at 0.824, a small gain. Early and late fusion land at the same level. Changing C, L2 norm, PCA, meta_weight, stacking or gating all gave changes within noise or made it worse. The remaining hard classes are Lepidic and Papillary (~0.73-0.75), and no knob has moved them. Seven more non-improving trials would end the search.
REASONING: Untested combiners for late fusion are mean_logit and learned_weights. mean_logit is a cheap, low-variance alternative to averaging probabilities. learned_weights could down-weight a weaker model, but its inner-CV weights are noisy with 134 patients, as stacking already showed. Early fusion with balance_blocks=False is also untested, but the C=0.001 early run already matched late fusion. mean_logit at the best C is the most plausible small gain with the least variance, though a clear accepted gain is unlikely.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.828-0.834, probably not accepted. If it is not accepted, the combine rule does not matter and fusion has plateaued near 0.83. Remaining trials should then go to untried early-fusion options (balance_blocks=False, PCA, C=0.01) before accepting that trial #1 is the final configuration.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion variant lands at 0.82-0.83 AUROC, about 0.006-0.007 above H-optimus-1 alone, and no change has cleared the noise threshold. For late fusion, C=0.01 is clearly best. L2 normalisation, PCA=64, a higher meta_weight, mean_logit and stacking were all neutral or worse. Early fusion at C=0.001 tied late fusion. Its other C values and PCA have not been tested.
REASONING: With 6 trials left before the stop rule, the most plausible untested source of a clear gain is early fusion with stronger dimensionality reduction. Concatenating three blocks of 1.5-2.5k dimensions from 134 patients is very noisy. PCA=32 per model, block balancing and a moderate C=0.01 let the joint classifier use cross-model interactions on a compact, denoised representation. Late fusion with PCA was neutral, but early fusion is the setting where a joint fit on fewer features should matter most.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.835-0.84, with gains on the weak classes Lepidic and Papillary. If it again ties near 0.83, I will conclude that fusion is saturated at roughly 0.83. I would then spend at most a couple more trials (learned_weights, or a strongly regularised gated model) before accepting trial #1.

ANALYSIS: All fusion variants cluster at 0.82-0.83 AUROC. That is about 0.006 above the best single model (hoptimus1, 0.8236). C=0.01 is clearly the best regularisation strength. Changes to PCA, L2 norm, the combine rule (mean_prob vs mean_logit) and early vs late fusion give differences of 0.001 or less, well inside noise. Stacking, gated fusion and a high meta_weight all hurt. That pattern fits added variance on 134 training patients per fold. Lepidic and Papillary (around 0.73-0.75) remain the weak classes in every variant.
REASONING: With 5 trials left before the stop rule, the most informative untested structural option is learned_weights. Equal weighting may under-use H-optimus-1, the strongest single model. Simplex weights have only 2 free parameters, so they are far less prone to overfitting than stack, which failed in trial #8. Keeping C=0.01 and the other knobs from the best trial isolates the effect of the combine rule.
EXPECTED: I expect a gain of 0.000-0.008 AUROC with weights tilted toward H-optimus-1, probably still below the acceptance threshold. If it is not accepted, I will conclude that the ensemble is at a plateau: the three foundation models carry largely redundant information at slide level, and weighting cannot extract more. The remaining trials then go to one or two low-cost checks (early fusion without balance_blocks, weighted_vote) before accepting trial #1 as final.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion trial sits on a plateau at about 0.82–0.83 AUROC. Late mean_prob/mean_logit at C=0.01 is the best, about 0.006 above the strongest single model, H-optimus-1. Changing the combiner, L2 normalisation, meta_weight, or PCA=64 at the same C made no difference. Stacking and learned weights did slightly worse, likely from inner-CV variance with only 134 training patients. Papillary (~0.72) and Lepidic (~0.74) remain the weak classes in every configuration.
REASONING: Only 4 trials remain before the patience stop, so the next one should probe an untested region rather than repeat neighbours. Strong PCA compression (16 components per model) together with weaker shrinkage (C=0.1) is a different bias-variance regime. PCA=64 at C=0.01 changed nothing, possibly because the C=0.01 shrinkage was doing all the work. Using mean_logit keeps the best combiner seen so far.
EXPECTED: If low-rank structure carries the class signal, AUROC should reach about 0.835–0.84, with gains on Papillary and Lepidic. If it lands at or below 0.83, the plateau is set by the information in mean-pooled embeddings rather than by the regularisation path. I would then conclude that fusion gives only a small, non-significant gain over H-optimus-1 and stop exploring this axis.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion variant sits on a plateau of about 0.82-0.83 AUROC, roughly 0.006 above the best single model (H-optimus-1). Late mean_prob/mean_logit at C=0.01 is the best region. C, PCA, L2 norm, meta_weight, stacking, learned weights and the one gated config all failed to clear the threshold. Strong compression (PCA 16) and stacking clearly hurt.
REASONING: Early fusion has only been run with no PCA at C=0.001, or with PCA 32 at C=0.01. Both were about 0.828-0.829, with the best balanced accuracy and better Lepidic/Acinar. balance_blocks divides each block by sqrt(columns), which shrinks the coefficients a lot. So without PCA the effective regularisation at C=0.001 was probably too strong. C=0.01 with full dimensions is the untested natural optimum for early fusion. With 3 trials left before the stop rule, this is the most plausible single change that could give a real gain.
EXPECTED: If it beats 0.835 with a consistent per-fold gain (Lepidic and Papillary up), early fusion at its proper regularisation is the winner. If it lands about 0.83 again, fusion is saturated at roughly +0.006 over H-optimus-1. Remaining trials would then add nothing, and the late mean_prob config #1 should stand as final.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion variant lands at 0.82–0.83 AUROC, which is only about 0.006 above the best single model (hoptimus1, 0.8236). No change to C, L2 normalisation, PCA, combine rule, meta_weight or method has come close to clearing the ~0.005–0.01 acceptance threshold. Strong regularisation (C≈0.01, or 0.001 for early fusion) is consistently best. Lepidic and Papillary stay at about 0.73–0.75 regardless of fusion, so the remaining error appears to be in the representations, not in how they are combined. Two non-improving trials remain before the search stops.
REASONING: The main untested direction with plausible upside is early fusion with all three settings that each looked mildly helpful: L2 normalisation, PCA 64, and C=0.001 (best for early fusion in #2). Combined, these could produce a different, more strongly regularised geometry than anything tried so far. Gated fusion is unlikely to win: it is noisy (threshold 0.012) and #7 was worse. Fine-tuning late fusion further would at best chase noise.
EXPECTED: Most likely AUROC of about 0.825–0.832, which would be rejected. If it is rejected, I conclude that fusion saturates near 0.83 and that trial #1 (simple late mean_prob, C=0.01) is the honest final choice. That gives roughly +0.006 over hoptimus1 alone, which may itself be within noise. A gain of more than ~0.006 would show that joint low-rank regularisation helps.

ANALYSIS: Fusion has plateaued at about 0.822-0.831 AUROC across early, late and gated methods. The accepted best (late mean_prob, C=0.01, 0.8298) is only about 0.006 above the best single model (H-optimus-1, 0.8236), so the gain from fusion is modest. No knob gave a gain above its noise threshold. Moving C away from 0.01, aggressive PCA, stacking and up-weighting metadata all hurt. Per-class profiles are nearly identical across trials (Papillary about 0.72, Lepidic about 0.74 are the weak classes).
REASONING: This is the last trial before the patience stop, so it should answer a still-open question rather than repeat a near-copy of the best. Every early-fusion trial so far used balance_blocks=True. The unbalanced variant has never been tested. Without block balancing, Virchow2 (2560 columns) dominates the concatenated input, so this tests whether letting the largest model dominate changes the fit. C=0.001 is the best early setting so far (#2, 0.8290).
EXPECTED: Most likely AUROC around 0.82-0.83 and a rejection, which would confirm that the three encoders are largely redundant at slide level. In that case the search ends with late mean_prob (#1) as the fused model. A clear gain (above about 0.005) would be surprising and would suggest that block balancing was diluting a useful signal.
